problems.source_says: Writing self-efficacy was measured by a self-report scale administered after the writing task. Section 3.2 explicitly establishes AI availability during essay writing, but neither it nor Figure 1 establishes AI availability during completion of the questionnaires. Under the codebook definition referring to production of the scored output, this yes is unsupported for the questionnaire outcome; availability during scale completion is unreported, and the output-production field is not applicable to this self-report. This does not imply AI was removed, and the existing question=none and scored_on_output=false classifications remain correct.
problems.quote: Upon completion of the writing task, both the Flow Status Scale and Writing Self-Efficacy Scale were immediately applied to all participants.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 meets criterion 3: three researchers evaluated the collected essays, and three raters independently applied a rubric to the written products. This is a researcher-rated output measure, not a self-report.

S1-O1 is overall_creativity: the total combines Originality (40 points), Flexibility (30), and Elaboration (30), for 100 points. Flexibility concerns angles within an essay, not diversity between people; only the total has reported group results.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; p. 7, Table 1 and Section 4.1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 is with_ai, with AI available during production and immediate timing: students used Deepseek during week-2 writing and handed in handwritten essays from that task. Later rating of those same essays does not make the outcome after_ai.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Sections 3.2-3.3 and Figure 1; p. 8, Section 4.4.

confirmed.statement: The reported analysis uses participant counts: Tables 1-3 each print N=20, 38, and 20. The peer arm contains 19 pairs, but the paper reports 38 observations for it; the form correctly preserves the paper's participant unit and notes the unresolved treatment of paired writing.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 5, Figure 1; p. 7, Tables 1-2; p. 8, Table 3.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 numbers match Table 1: GenAI 88.850 (SD 1.420, N=20), peer 86.825 (SD 2.719, N=38), individual 85.133 (SD 2.120, N=20); F=13.095, p=0.000***, partial eta-squared=0.259, Cohen's f=0.591. The note is ***p<0.001, and LSD lists a>b, a>c, b>c; neither AI contrast has a separately printed pairwise statistic.

S1-O1 rating details match: Kendall concordance is 0.57 in week 1 and 0.89 in week 2; the averaging rule applies when reliability is high, and the discussion to unanimous consensus is described for week 1. Blinding is not stated.

S1-O2 is correctly marked self_report, scored_on_output=false, and question=none: the six-point scale assesses confidence in ideation, conventions, and self-regulation. It is an immediate participant questionnaire, not a creativity score on the essay.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 2.3; p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Section 3.3; p. 7, Table 2.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 numbers match Table 2: GenAI 5.276 (SD 0.342, N=20), peer 5.022 (SD 0.756, N=38), individual 4.812 (SD 0.708, N=20); Welch F=4.106, p=0.023*, partial eta-squared=0.062, Cohen's f=0.256. The note is *p<0.05; LSD lists a>c, and the text says the GenAI-peer difference is not significant.

S1-O3 is correctly marked self_report, scored_on_output=false, and question=none: the eight-item, five-point scale assesses participants' flow, including control and enjoyment. It is an immediate participant questionnaire, not an output rating.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Section 3.3; p. 8, Table 3.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 numbers match Table 3: GenAI 3.919 (SD 0.441, N=20), peer 4.428 (SD 0.540, N=38), individual 4.031 (SD 0.635, N=20); F=6.974, p=0.002**, partial eta-squared=0.157, Cohen's f=0.431. The note is **p<0.01; LSD lists b>c and b>a, and the text says the GenAI-individual difference is not significant.

No additional qualifying outcome was found in the complete 13-page document. The unaided essay precedes the intervention; there is no post-removal creative task or cross-person diversity analysis. Table 4 codes prompt functions and uptake of AI content within student-AI episodes, not creativity or similarity between different participants' outputs.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because three researchers scored essays that students produced with AI available. The two self-report outcomes have unsupported AI-availability codes, while their exclusion from the three research questions is correct and all reported table statistics match the PDF.
